name: Wedge Drop

card.context: A stock under its 200-day (B26) bounces inside a downtrend, the way a bear-market rally makes a lower high, and stalls for a few days on or just above its 10 and 20-day EMAs. The index is in its own down cycle. Above the 200-day the same event is only a sell signal for a long.
card.pattern: A top (an extension, a lower high, or a failed push past the prior day's high), then a stall of 3 to 10 sessions hugging the 10-day EMA with quiet up days and no new high in the last 3. The averages catch up to price.
card.trigger: OTHER: the first daily close under both the 10 and 20-day EMAs, under the stall low, in the lower 40% of the day's range. Short at market in the last 15 minutes or at the next open.
card.stop: A few cents over the trigger day's high, or over the higher of the trigger day and the day before, within about 3%. Wider than that: skip or size down, never pull it in.
card.failure_mode: The drop is reclaimed: a close back above both averages within a few sessions (38% of the app's events within 3). Early in a new bull market, or in a strong leader, the bounce keeps going and the stop over the day's high is taken at once.

criteria.statement: Two jobs. Every long holder treats it as a sell signal. It is a short only in the narrow form below the 200-day, in a weak market.

measure.what: how the course uses the Wedge Drop
value: a sell signal for a long

options.basis: only a sell or stay-out signal for longs
only a short (the Model Book files it so)
both, the short only under B26 (the dossier's recommendation)

criteria.evidence: Kell uses it first as an exit: 'allow the wedge drop to protect you and take you out of the trade' (his March 2024 deck). 13 of the 15 source-marked examples sat above the 200-day, so most textbook cases are sell signals for us.

criteria.statement: For the short, the trigger day's close is under the 200-day SMA. The sell signal for a long has no 200-day test.
criteria.evidence: A hard rule ('200SMA is hardened rule yes'). 70% of the app's 99,695 Wedge Drops and 13 of 15 marked examples were above it. Test: above the 200-day -0.13R; below it -0.01R; below it with QQQ under its 50-day +0.29R.

criteria.statement: Prefer a falling 200-day: lower than it was 20 sessions ago.
criteria.evidence: The dossier says 'prefer a falling 200-day' and fixes no window; the 20 sessions mirror the pilot's rising test and are flagged for the owner. Scan: a falling 200-day on 437 of 618 hits, 26.5% to 3R against 24.3% overall. VALE 2026-09-14 was rejected for a rising 200-day.

criteria.statement: A prior up-move: at least 8 of the 10 closes before the trigger day were above the 20-day EMA.

measure.what: closes above the 20-day EMA in the 10 sessions before the trigger day

criteria.evidence: The app's own threshold (v44_read.cycle_events). For the short this is a bounce inside a downtrend: Kell's 'faster rallies that would put in a lower high', the owner's 'decent pop back up and rejection coinciding with the 50SMA or 20EMA' (Sunday Scans 2026-11-01).

criteria.statement: The bounce made a top: an extension, a lower high, or a failed push past the prior day's high. At least one of the three.

value: failed push past the prior day's high

criteria.evidence: The three shapes are Kell's (the Exhaustion Extension; the bear-market lower high; 'If prices can't push past the previous day's highs, especially after several attempts'); the tests are the dossier's. Scan: lower-high tops 483 hits, 25.3% to 3R; failed-push-only 58, 25.9%; extension tops 120, 15.0%.

criteria.statement: An extension top: a close at least 2.5 ATR over the 20-day EMA in the last 20 sessions, or about 4% or more over the 10-day for an index.

measure.what: highest (close - 20-day EMA) / ATR(14) in the last 20 sessions
measure.or: an index close 4% or more over its 10-day EMA

criteria.evidence: The 4% is Kell's QQQ note ('4-5% above the Daily 10EMA'); the 2.5 ATR is the dossier's number. An extension that is itself a parabolic burst is the Parabolic Short's trade, taken on the climax day, not this one. Scan: extension tops did worst, 15.0% to 3R. CAT 2018-10-09 (a 3.9-ATR extension) is the one extension example.

criteria.statement: A lower-high top: the bounce peaks under the highest high of the 60 sessions before it. The A+ form, the owner's pop and rejection at the 50-day or 20-day.

measure.what: top high against the highest high of the 60 sessions before the top

criteria.evidence: The 60 sessions is the scan's reading of 'the bounce peaks under the prior high'. Scan: 483 of 618 hits, 25.3% to 3R, the best of the three tops. Nine of the ten examples are lower highs (WHR, PCG, GS at the falling 50-day or 20-day EMA).

criteria.statement: The stall: 3 to 10 sessions between the top and the trigger day.

measure.what: sessions from the top to the trigger day

criteria.evidence: Kell: 'the price will trade tight into the moving averages as there are now fewer new buyers'; the count is the dossier's. The ten examples' stalls ran 3 to 7 days; Kell's own QQQ stall ran about 2 weeks.

criteria.statement: Through the stall no close is more than 1 ATR from the 10-day EMA.

measure.what: largest |close - 10-day EMA| / ATR(14) over the stall

criteria.evidence: Kell's 'tight range as moving averages catch up'. The ten examples' stalls were 2.7% to 7.1% wide (INCY the tightest at 2.7%); MELI 2026-02-03 (9.8%) and EOG 2019-09-24 (8.4%) were rejected as wide and loose.

criteria.statement: No new high in the last 3 sessions of the stall.

measure.what: highest high of the last 3 sessions against the top

criteria.statement: In the stall the up days come on lighter volume than the down days.

measure.what: average volume of the stall's up days / average volume of its down days

criteria.evidence: Kell's pages list 'Decreased buying volume (accumulation)' and 'Increased selling volume (distribution)'. The Model Book's 'volume dries up through the wedge' keeps only half of that; the heavy-selling half is the one that matters.

criteria.statement: Wide, loose action before the drop is graded down, not excluded.
criteria.evidence: TraderLion's NVDA 2023 chart labels 'Wide And Loose Price Action' and still marks a Wedge Drop out of it. DXCM 2022-04-18: an 8-day stall 9.6% wide, a 2.4% stop, stopped the next session, then the stock fell 37%.

criteria.statement: The stall sits on or just above the averages. A bounce into the underside of falling averages is the next stage, the downside EMA Crossback, not this setup.

options.basis: Kell's: a stall on or above rising averages, then the first close under both
the Model Book's: a rising wedge under the averages

criteria.evidence: Kell's drawings and TraderLion's META, AAPL and ANF charts stall on or just above rising averages. The Model Book's 'beneath the averages' is a machine mirror of the Wedge Pop text (commit 3aa9b1eeaf, 2026-06-17), not the owner's words; you cannot lose averages you are already under.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day on average.
criteria.evidence: Kell's own long screen is stricter on price ($20, Deepvue). The scan used the house floor; 2,630 names ever qualified.

criteria.statement: Easy to borrow at a fair fee.
criteria.evidence: Not testable on our data; the test charged no borrow fees.

criteria.statement: The trigger averages are the 10 and 20-day EMAs, Kell's pair. The trail uses the house 10 and 21-day.

options.basis: Kell's own pair, on his cycle page and his posts
the Model Book card
the app's Chart IQ v3 rule
the house trail, E52

criteria.evidence: It is Kell's term, so the trigger should match his: '10 and 20-day exponential moving averages guide us through the intermediate-term trend'. The EMA Crossback dossier (14) reaches the same point; one ruling settles both.

criteria.statement: The first daily close under both the 10 and 20-day EMAs after the stall.

measure.what: close against the 10-day EMA and the 20-day EMA, the day before not under both

options.basis: a close under the 10 counts (Kell's QQQ 2023-02-16/17 and AMD 2024-01-02 exit)
both are required (TraderLion's ANF 'broke below both moving averages'; the app's rule)

criteria.evidence: Kell and Deepvue say 'below the moving averages'; 'both, on a daily close' is the dossier's stricter reading. Kell's own dated calls came on closes under the 10-day only, and his NVDA tweet was posted mid-session. The 10-only version was not measured. For the long holder's exit (a) is closer to what Kell did.

criteria.statement: A close under the 10-day only is 'wedge drop ish': enough to sell a long, graded down as a short.
criteria.evidence: UCT on QQQ 2025-11-04: 'it was a wedge drop ish day with the gap down and sell on Tuesday!' (under the 10-day only). Kell acted on a 10-only loss twice.

criteria.statement: The trigger day closes in the lower 40% of its range.
criteria.evidence: The app's threshold. The A+ picture is a wide red bar or a gap down closing near its low (CAH 2009, TSM 2022, GEN 2025 all dropped on gaps).

criteria.statement: The trigger day closes under the low of the stall (the pivot).

measure.what: close against the stall's lowest low

options.basis: the close under both averages only
also under the stall low (the dossier's recommendation)
an intraday break on the 65-minute chart

criteria.evidence: Kell's own triggers were price levels ('officially triggered a wedge drop today through that 790 pivot area'; 'If lost 166.50 would trigger a wedge drop short sale'). Using the stall low mirrors the Wedge Pop's 'Consolidation sets the level to trade against'. The scan required it; the trigger level of each example is its stall low.

criteria.statement: Trigger-day volume at least the 50-day average; 1.5x or more, or a gap down, is the strong form. A grade cue, not a gate.

options.basis: a hard gate at the 50-day average
a hard gate at 1.5x
a grading cue (the dossier's recommendation)

criteria.evidence: Kell's pages: 'increased selling pressure', 'influx of sellers', ANF 'on increased volume'. Test: 1.5x or more raised the win rate (34% against 29%) but not the average R (-0.08R against -0.09R); scan: 1.5x on 39 hits, 25.6%, no better. DIS 2006-01-26 came on 3.3x and failed; GEN 2025-12-31 dropped on 0.4x and ran 18R.

criteria.statement: A market order in the last 15 minutes once the close under both averages is clear, or at the next open.

value: the last 15 minutes of the trigger day

criteria.evidence: E57 gives the market order; the timing is the dossier's. The test and the scan shorted the trigger day's close. E58 keeps it in regular hours.

criteria.statement: Advanced: an intraday break of the stall low on the 65-minute chart counts only once the daily close confirms it.

measure.what: intraday break of the stall low
measure.value: confirmed by the daily close under both averages

criteria.evidence: Kell: 'Try to get In on the 65 minute' (his slide on long breakouts); 'Hourly and 15-minute charts are for timing entries.' His 65-minute QQQ read: 'We had the Wedge Drop, followed through down on 297/298'.

criteria.statement: No short more than 4% under the trigger level.
criteria.evidence: C28 mirrored through D47. The scan skipped hits more than 4% under the stall low.

criteria.statement: Skip a short more than 10% under its 10-day average. Check it at the open on a gap down.
criteria.evidence: C29 is written for longs; the dossier mirrors it through D47. A big gap down can open far under the 10-day.

criteria.statement: A few cents over the trigger day's high, or over the higher of the trigger day and the day before.

measure.value: a few cents over the trigger day's high, or over the 2-day high

options.basis: the house default, A3 and F62 mirrored; median 2.7% away
the house alternative (the prior day's low, mirrored); median 4.2% away
TraderLion's 'a stop just above the recent high'; the Model Book's wedge high; often outside 3%

options.value: the day's high or the 2-day high, within 3%
options.basis: the dossier's recommendation: either, so long as it fits A13

criteria.recommended: the day's high or the 2-day high, within 3%
criteria.evidence: The scan used $0.03 over the 2-day high, the day's high alone when that was more than 3% away, no trade past 3%. The wider stops did not improve results: in the best regime +0.29R with the day-high stop fell to -0.02R with the 2-day high. META 2022-01-05 shows the other side: stopped at -1R, then down 27% in 20 sessions.

criteria.statement: If the stop is more than about 3% away, skip or take the smaller size the rules give. Never pull it in.
criteria.evidence: 56% of the app's events fit 3% with the day-high stop, 29% with the 2-day high. Gap-down and wide-range drops run wide: TSLA 2023-07-20 (a 4% gap) 6.9%, ANF 2024-03-08 (an 8% range day) 8.8%. DXCM 2026-03-05 sat right at 3.0%.

criteria.statement: Not the 15-bar high (the app's kell_cycle level) or the top of a wide stall, unless that fits 3%.

measure.what: (stop - entry) / entry, with the stop at the 15-bar high or the stall top

criteria.evidence: kell_cycle.py puts the stop 1% over the 15-bar high, often far wider than 3%.

criteria.statement: A gap up through the stop: the first 30-minute high is the new stop; out if the loss passes 2R.

measure.what: loss at the first 30-minute high of the gap-up day

criteria.evidence: 10.5% of the test's trades left through a gap over the stop; the worst was -12.8R. It matters more on shorts.

criteria.statement: Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first cover by default.

measure.what: R at which the stop moves to the entry

criteria.statement: Cover a third at 3R.
criteria.evidence: Among the ten examples 3R came in 3 to 21 sessions (EXP in 3, INCY in 21).

criteria.statement: Cover a third at 5R.
If it opens past a cover level, take that cover at the open.
Trail the last third: cover on a close back above the 10-day EMA for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one.
criteria.evidence: Kell gives no targets. He expects a rally into the falling averages (the downside EMA Crossback), then lower; covering on a close back over the 10-day fits that. The test trailed the rest after the first cover on a close above the 10-day EMA.

criteria.statement: Under 1R of profit after 10 sessions: cover.
criteria.evidence: Applied in the test. INCY 2023-08-17 was the slowest example (3R on day 21): the grind down the 10-day EMA, taught as the case for patience inside the rule.

criteria.statement: What Kell expects next: a rally into the falling averages, the downside EMA Crossback. A rally that stalls under the falling 10 and 20-day is a place to hold, not to panic; the trail still covers on a close back above the 10 or 21-day.

measure.what: rally high against the falling 10-day and 20-day EMAs

criteria.evidence: Kell: 'an EMA Crossback to the downside will retest the moving averages but is now met with more resistance, pushing the stock lower.' The 'hold, not panic' is the dossier's.

criteria.statement: Do not add at the crossback. That is a new trade with its own stop.
criteria.evidence: Kell's Downside EMA Crossback page says to add there; A5 says one price, one stop, and B21 makes the crossback a new trade.

criteria.statement: A close back above both the 10 and 20-day EMAs: cover.
criteria.evidence: Kell: 'If the stock regains its moving averages and pushes higher, exit the short position.' UCT lets a Wedge Drop be 'invalidated' within days (QQQ 2025-08-29: 'unless immediately invalidated early next week'; back over both by 09-04). Test: 38% of the app's events did this within 3 sessions, 54.5% within 5; scan 37.9%.

criteria.statement: A close above the trigger day's high: the stop has already gone; the stop is the exit.
For the long holder, the mirror: a Wedge Drop reclaimed within a few sessions was a shakeout. Buy again only on a new setup, as a new trade.
criteria.evidence: Kell re-bought MU at the next EMA Crossback ('A few days after the Wedge Drop took out the first trade, MU found support at the EMA Crossback level').

criteria.statement: For the short: the index in its own down cycle, QQQ under its 50-day SMA and its 20-day EMA; the market reading Orange or Red.

measure.what: QQQ close against its 50-day SMA and 20-day EMA on the trigger day

options.basis: the house reading only (F65)
also require QQQ under its 50-day (the dossier's recommendation, the only regime with a measured edge)

criteria.evidence: Test: under the 200-day with QQQ under its 50-day was the only regime with an edge (+0.29R on 9,197 trades; Wedge Drop stocks lagged the base rate by 1.4 points over 20 sessions there, +0.14% against +1.52%). The 20-day EMA half was not measured. The scan required QQQ under its 50-day on every hit, so its base rate says nothing about a strong market.

criteria.statement: RS rating 20 or less, in a weak group; the stock lags the market.
criteria.evidence: C31's short mirror. Textbook Wedge Drops happen in leaders (70% of the app's events had a positive 63-day return, 52% had beaten QQQ); the B26-compliant form is naturally lower RS. A leader with strong RS is a B- as a short. The scan cannot read an RS rating.

criteria.statement: Not early in a new bull market, not in a strongly uptrending stock, and not too late in the fall.
criteria.evidence: TraderLion under Kell's byline: 'avoid shorting early in new bull markets or strong uptrending stocks'; 'Be careful not to short too late in the downtrend, just like buying late in an uptrend.' GOOGL 2019-01-14: a textbook hit a few weeks after the December 2018 low with QQQ still under its 50-day; stopped the next session, +7.2% twenty sessions later.

criteria.statement: No new short in the 3 sessions before a report. A Wedge Drop that is the earnings reaction itself is allowed, after the report.
criteria.evidence: AAPL 2023-08-04 and TSLA 2023-07-20 were earnings reactions. A report inside the first two weeks belongs in the checklist: DIS 2006-01-26 took the stop on its reaction day (2006-02-07); CAT 2018 reached 3R before its report added the gap.

criteria.statement: The B26 parabolic exception never covers a Wedge Drop. A short above the 200-day after a blow-off is the Parabolic Short, on its climax day, with its own checklist.

measure.what: B26's parabolic exception applies to a Wedge Drop

options.basis: never applies to a Wedge Drop (the dossier's recommendation; DECISIONS D-040's default)
applies when the run before it met Bracco's parabolic-burst checklist

criteria.evidence: Bracco's parabolic short is a climax-day trade that ends at the 9-day EMA; a Wedge Drop comes days or weeks later, back at the averages, where his trade is already over. DECISIONS D-040's default: a Wedge Drop never qualifies.

criteria.statement: Job 1: the index's own Wedge Drop (QQQ or SPY under both its EMAs) is a reason to cut long exposure, in any market.
criteria.evidence: Kell's page: 'when an index like the S&P 500 or Nasdaq forms a Wedge Drop, it's a warning that the market as a whole is weakening.' Bracco 2025-12-14: 'Nasdaq wedge dropped on Friday ... Looks like this is the start of another leg down/pullback'. SMH 2026-07-02 and RSP 2026-08-31 were UCT index calls.

measure.what: index close against its 10-day and 20-day EMAs

criteria.statement: For a long holder the Wedge Drop is the last exit: if the second extension did not take you out, this does.
criteria.evidence: Kell's deck: 'If you don't sell the second extension or it doesn't materialize allow the wedge drop to protect you and take you out of the trade.' His AMD exit: 'A gap down through the moving averages is more than enough for Oliver to exit the trade.'

a_plus: wd.top_lower_high: a bounce into the 50-day or 20-day that makes a lower high, the owner's pop and rejection
wd.market: QQQ under its 50-day; wd.weak_group: a weak group
wd.stall_length: a tight stall of 3 to 10 days hugging the 10-day EMA (wd.stall_tight) with quiet up days (wd.stall_volume)
wd.trigger_close: a wide red bar or a gap down closing near its low (wd.close_position), under both averages and under the stall low (wd.under_stall_low)
wd.stop_width: the stop over the day's high within 3%
wd.not_new_bull: not late in the fall
b_minus: wd.wide_loose: wide, loose action before the drop
wd.ten_only_graded_down: a close under the 10-day only, as a short (enough as an exit for a long)
wd.market: an index in an uptrend
wd.weak_group: a leader with strong RS
wd.not_new_bull: a stock already far below its averages, late in the fall
wd.top_extension: an extension top (15.0% to 3R in the scan)
wd.trigger_close: the 20-day lost a day after the 10, average volume, or the index only flat (an A or B)
no_trade: wd.below_200: above the 200-day, a sell signal for a long and not a short at all
wd.parabolic_exception: a blow-off top shorted above the 200-day is the Parabolic Short's trade, not this one
wd.stall_on_averages: the stall sits under the averages (a downside EMA Crossback, the next stage)
wd.no_chase: more than 4% under the trigger level
wd.not_stretched: more than 10% under the 10-day average
wd.stop_width: the honest stop does not fit 3%; never pull it in
wd.liquidity: under $10 or under $20 million a day; wd.borrow: hard to borrow
wd.market: a Green or Yellow reading, or early in a new bull market (wd.not_new_bull)

lookalikes.tell: Look where price sits before the day and which way it closes through the averages. A Wedge Pop coils under the 10 and 20-day EMAs and closes up through both; a Wedge Drop stalls on or just above them and closes down through both.

Measure the distance to the averages on the trigger day. A Parabolic Short is shorted on the climax day of a 3 to 5 day burst, 10% or more over the 9-day EMA; a Wedge Drop comes days later, after a stall within 1 ATR of the 10-day EMA.

Ask which side of the averages the bounce came from. A downside EMA Crossback is a rally from under the falling averages that stalls at their underside; a Wedge Drop's stall sits on or above them, and the drop is the first close under both.

Count the quiet days. The mean-reversion short sells the turn of a stretched rally (3 or more straight up days, a close 3 ATR over the 20-day) on the day it turns; a Wedge Drop needs 3 to 10 sessions stalled on the averages first, then the close through them.

invalidations: Before the trigger: the stall makes a new high in its last 3 sessions, or a close sits more than 1 ATR from the 10-day EMA (wd.stall_no_new_high, wd.stall_tight).
Before the trigger: a close back above the 200-day (wd.below_200).
Before the trigger: a report within 3 sessions, wait (wd.earnings).
After the entry: a close back above both the 10 and 20-day EMAs, cover (wd.inv_reclaim).
After the entry: a close above the trigger day's high; the stop is the exit (wd.inv_stop).
After the entry: under 1R of profit after 10 sessions, cover (wd.time_stop).
For the long holder: a Wedge Drop reclaimed within a few sessions was a shakeout; buy again only on a new setup (wd.inv_shakeout_long).
mistakes: Shorting a leader at its highs because it lost the 10-day once. It breaks B26, and the sources warn against strong uptrends.
Shorting the blow-off itself. That is the Parabolic Short, a different setup with its own checklist.
Shorting inside the stall before the close confirms.
Treating a cross of the averages as the whole setup. Kell on the mirror: 'Many traders mistakenly believe the Wedge Pop is simply about crossing the moving averages.'
A stop too tight in a volatile name. META 2022-01-05 stopped out at -1R, then fell 27% within 20 sessions; DXCM 2022-04-18 the same, then down 37%. 'As stocks trend down, volatility increases.'
Late to the party: 'Be careful not to short too late in the downtrend'.
Holding a long through it. The drop is the last exit, not a reason to hope.
Adding at the crossback. A5 says no; the crossback can be a new trade (B21).
Shorting a few weeks after a market low with the index still under its 50-day (GOOGL 2019-01-14): the 'early in new bull markets' case.
Taking the app's kell_cycle levels or its quotes as Kell's. The detector fires on 100% of charts, has the wrong cycle order and the wrong book title.

short_mirror.note: The Wedge Drop is itself the short mirror of the Wedge Pop (Kell's own pairing; D47). Its own long side, read as an exit, is to sell the long on the Wedge Drop: 'allow the wedge drop to protect you and take you out of the trade.' Whether the short is taught is D-001.

best_conditions: For the short: the index in a down cycle (QQQ under its 50-day and 20-day EMA), the reading Orange or Red, the stock under a falling 200-day in a weak group, the bounce rejected at the 50-day or 20-day. Not early in a new bull market, not late in the fall. For the sell signal: any market; the index's own Wedge Drop is a reason to cut exposure.

management.trail: cover the last third on a close back above the 10-day EMA for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first cover by default (B19)
management.time_stop: under 1R of profit after 10 sessions, cover (C33)
management.gap_open: a cover level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: a gap up through the stop: the first 30-minute high is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.overrides: none. The setup keeps the house defaults (8.4); a rally that stalls under the falling averages is a place to hold, not to add (A5, B21). Not ours: the Downside EMA Crossback page's add at the crossback, kell_cycle.py's entry 0.1% under the 15-bar low and stop 1% over the 15-bar high, and the classical rising-wedge measured move (ChartSchool says there is none).

base_rate.window: 60 sessions forward, fixed stop, no trims, no breakeven, no trail, no time stop; 1999-04 to 2026-11; QQQ under its 50-day required on every hit; one hit per name per 20 sessions

app_rule_test_2008_2026.note: the app's own 'Wedge drop' events, house short, 2008 to 2026, survivors only

failures.why: a lower-high top, a three-day stall 3.4% wide, a 2.1% stop; stopped the next session at 0R; twenty sessions later 7.2% above the entry. A few weeks after the December 2018 low with QQQ still under its 50-day: the early-in-a-new-bull-market case.

an extension-plus-failed-push top, an 8-day stall 9.6% wide, a 2.4% stop; stopped the next session at 0R, then the stock fell 37% within 20 sessions. A stop that fits 3% can be the wrong stop in a volatile name; the move you then miss is not evidence the entry was right.

a failed-push top, a three-day stall, trigger volume 3.3x the 50-day average (the strong form); never past 0.34R, stopped on day 8, its earnings reaction day, and 11.6% above the entry twenty sessions later. Heavy volume is a cue, not a gate, and a report inside the first two weeks belongs in the checklist.
B26-compliant (4% under the 200-day), a 3.6% stop; stopped at -1R, then down 27.3% within 20 sessions. The tight-stop risk in a volatile name.

Kell's own short trigger ('If lost 166.50'), 19% under the 200-day, a 2.1% stop; lost 1R and the stock rose 55.5% over the next 20 sessions. He had flagged it 'a laggard name. Might just be an avoid'; a strong uptrending market and the stock's own 2023 recovery ran it over.

a lower high under the 200-day, a 3-day stall 3.2% wide, a 2.4% stop; stopped on day 2 at 0R when the close reclaimed both EMAs (a shakeout); the slide through the 5R level came in July without the trade.

examples.limits: The RS rating, the group, the market reading and the owner's grade are not in the scan. Survivors only, which biases every short result downward. Some same-day clusters (2011-08-02, 2022-06-08 to 06-10) are one market event counted many times. Best R is the deepest point before the stop, not a realised result. Nothing here is a published statistic.

near_misses.why: the trigger close is 8.3% above the 200-day SMA: a sell signal for a long in an uptrend, not a short; 0.93R then stopped as the stock made new highs.
a stall close sat 1.42 ATR from the 10-day EMA (rule: 1 ATR or less): an extension turn with no real stall, the mean-reversion short, not a Wedge Drop.
the trigger day closed at 56% of its range (rule: the lower 40%): an undecided close under the averages; stopped at 0R.
the stall's up days averaged 2.84x the volume of its down days (rule: under 1x): accumulation, not distribution; 0.54R then stopped.

question_seeds.seed: Which two averages must the stock close under on the trigger day, and whose pair are they?
Above the 200-day, what is a Wedge Drop for us: a short, or something else?
Where does the stop go on a Wedge Drop short, and how far away may it be?
Hidden ticker: tap the stall low, the level the trigger day must close under.
Hidden ticker: which of these four stalls hugs the 10-day EMA within 1 ATR for 3 to 10 days?
Hidden ticker: is this bounce a lower high under the falling 50-day, or a new high? Short candidate or pass.
Wedge Drop or Wedge Pop: price just closed through both EMAs. Which side was it on before, and which way did it close?
Wedge Drop or Parabolic Short: the stock is 25% over its 9-day EMA on a gap-up day that closes red. Which is it?
Wedge Drop or downside EMA Crossback: the bounce came from under the falling averages and stalled at their underside. Which stage is this?
You shorted the close under both averages. Two days later it closes back above both, under your stop. What now?
The trigger day gaps down and opens 12% under its 10-day average. Short at the open, or pass?
A textbook stall breaks under both averages, but QQQ is above its 50-day and the reading is Green. Short, or sell signal only?
Same stall, two drops: one on 0.7x volume closing mid-range, one a gap down on 1.8x closing at the low. Grade each.
An 8-day stall 9.6% wide breaks down under both averages with a 2.4% stop. A+, B-, or pass?
Short at 55.16 with the stop at 56.28. How far is the stop in percent, and does it fit the 3% rule?
Shorted at 45.96 with the stop at 46.89. Where is 3R?
Of the 10 closes before the trigger day, 7 were above the 20-day EMA. Does the prior bounce qualify?

conflicts: Sources: the dossier's section 11 lists its sources by name and link with no numbers, so the card cites them by position in reading order (S1 the 2021-03-06 tweet ... S22 Bulkowski, S23 to S25 the UCT posts, S26 to S32 the repo files), the reader the validator uses for unnumbered dossiers.

Which averages: 10/20 EMA (Kell), 9/20 (the Model Book), 9/21 (Chart IQ v3), 10/21 (the house trail). The card takes 10/20 for the trigger and the house 10/21 for the trail (D-021; the EMA Crossback dossier asks the same).

One average or both: Kell called QQQ 2023-02-16/17 and exited AMD 2024-01-02 on a loss of the 10 only; TraderLion's ANF caption and the app require both. The card requires both for the short and grades a 10-only loss down (D-078). The 10-only version was not measured.

Where the stall sits: on or just above the averages (Kell's drawings, TraderLion's examples) against 'beneath the averages' (the Model Book card and playbook, a machine mirror of the Wedge Pop text, commit 3aa9b1eeaf). The card takes Kell's; the playbook's 'after a topping move or Reversal Extension' is a mirroring error (a Reversal Extension is Kell's bottom).
Trigger: a price level (Kell's tweets: '790 pivot', '166.50') against the averages (TraderLion, the app). The card takes both: a close under both averages and under the stall low (D-003).

Stop: the day's high (house) against 'just above the recent high' (TraderLion) and the wedge high (the Model Book). The card takes the day's high or the 2-day high within 3%; wider stops did not improve the test (D-008).
Role: Kell uses it first as an exit; the Model Book files it as a short. The card teaches both, the short only under B26 (D-001).
Volume: 'increased selling pressure' (TraderLion) against 'dries up' (the Model Book). The card: quiet up days in the stall, heavier volume on the drop; a cue, not a gate (D-006).

The 200-day: 70% of the app's Wedge Drops and 13 of 15 source-marked examples sit above it; B26 forbids those shorts. The measured edge lives only below the 200-day with QQQ under its 50-day (+0.29R), and even there it fell to -0.02R with the 2-day stop: thin, and dependent on the stop.
The parabolic exception: the dossier recommends it never covers a Wedge Drop; DECISIONS D-040 agrees. A Wedge Drop after a burst is graded as a Wedge Drop, not shorted above the 200-day.

App text not to teach: kell_cycle.py's Stage 4 levels, its invented Kell quotes ('size the Wedge Drop trade larger than your Wedge Pop ...') and its wrong book title ('Victorious Stock Operator'; Open Library lists Victory in Stock Trading); the Study F2 bank's 'RED LIGHT (Below 20 EMA): Stay in CASH' line shown as Kell's words (no source found); the v3 rule's 50-day condition, which excludes most of Kell's examples (D-010).

Course sourcing: SET.17 plans losing examples from failed classical rising wedges, a different months-long pattern (Bulkowski: 3 weeks minimum, five touches each line). The card's failures are failed Kell-style Wedge Drops from the scan instead.
The scan's 'falling 200-day' cut names no window; the card's wd.falling_200 borrows the pilot's 20 sessions and says so.
The exit rule on a reclaim (wd.inv_reclaim) is Kell's line (S11) and UCT's own 'invalidated' reading (QQQ 2025-08-29, S25); the card tags it originator.
